W sklepie papryka czerwienieje przez jedną noc, a olej ze smażalni jedzie do oczyszczenia i wraca z powrotem do frytek. Rozmawiamy o tym, ile białka potrzebuje rosnące dziecko i dlaczego dieta planetarna w szkołach budzi tyle sprzeciwu, skoro dzieci w tym wieku rosną najszybciej. Pytamy o glifosat, aspartam i dwa tysiące dodatków do żywności, bo każdy z nich bada się osobno, a nikt nie sprawdza, co robią razem. videos.title: Emocje, które zasłaniają nam możliwości
videos.description:
Czy zdarzyło Ci się kiedyś nie dostrzegać żadnego rozwiązania, a po pewnym czasie zastanawiać się, dlaczego wcześniej go nie widziałeś?

Emocje wpływają na sposób, w jaki postrzegamy rzeczywistość. 
Na to, jakie możliwości dostrzegamy, z których rezygnujemy i jakie podejmujemy decyzje.

Podczas kolejnego spotkania w Klubie 555 Fryderyk Karzełek i Bartosz Sitkiewicz porozmawiają o tym:

• Jak emocje ograniczają naszą zdolność dostrzegania nowych możliwości?
• Dlaczego w trudnych sytuacjach tak często nie widzimy alternatyw?
• Jak odzyskać umiejętność widzenia twórczej perspektywy, nie rezygnując z prawa do przeżywania emocji?
• Jak trenować tę kompetencję w codziennym życiu?

Być może nie potrzebujesz dzisiaj nowych możliwości. Potrzebujesz dostrzec te, których do tej pory nie widziałeś.

O 5:55 inspirująca rozmowa

Fryderyk

videos.title: Dlaczego stoisz w miejscu, mimo że tak bardzo chcesz ruszyć?
videos.description:
Masz w głowie pomysł. Nawet wiesz, jaki powinien być Twój pierwszy krok. 

Otwierasz kalendarz. Przesuwasz zadanie na jutro. Potem na kolejny tydzień. W międzyczasie pojawia się coś pilniejszego, coś ważniejszego… i znowu mija kolejny miesiąc. 

Brzmi znajomo? 

Czasem najtrudniejsze nie jest wymyślenie, co zrobić. Najtrudniejsze jest przejście od myślenia do działania. Dlaczego tak się dzieje? I co właściwie nas wtedy zatrzymuje? 

O tym porozmawiamy już jutro - na żywo, w wyjątkowym gronie. 

🔥 Do rozmowy dołączą: 

Fryderyk Karzełek 
Aldona Danielska 
Anna Oszajca 
Magdalena Daniłoś 

Cztery osoby, różne perspektywy i jeden temat: dlaczego stoisz w miejscu, mimo że tak bardzo chcesz ruszyć? 

Nie zdradzimy Ci wszystkiego teraz. 😉 Warto być z nami na żywo!

videos.title: Na pewno się nie da?
videos.description:
Ile Twoich decyzji zapadło w chwili, gdy ktoś rzucił „nie da się”, a nikt nie dopytał, czego dokładnie się nie da? 

W tym odcinku przyjrzymy się temu, skąd bierze się pewność, że wyczerpaliśmy wszystkie możliwości. Pokażę Ci, jak odróżnić ograniczenie, które trzeba uszanować, od warunku, który można zmienić. 

Zobaczysz też, jak te same zasoby mogą dać zupełnie nowy efekt, kiedy zadasz sobie inne pytanie. 

Weź ze sobą jedną sprawę, którą odłożyłeś jako niemożliwą, bo podczas spotkania zrobimy z niej ćwiczenie.

Gdzie sprawdzić plan ogólny gminy?
Zacznij od strony gminy, jej Biuletynu Informacji Publicznej (BIP) i ogłoszeń o pracach nad planem. Sprawdź, czy dostępny dokument to projekt, czy uchwalony plan. Odszukaj swoją działkę na mapie i sprawdź jej strefę planistyczną.

Kiedy złożyć wniosek, a kiedy uwagi do planu ogólnego?
Wniosek do projektu składa się w czasie naboru wniosków ogłoszonego przez gminę. Uwagi do projektu składa się podczas konsultacji społecznych. Termin i sposób złożenia pisma znajdziesz w ogłoszeniu gminy.

Jak napisać uwagi do planu ogólnego?
Podaj dane działki, wskaż proponowaną strefę i uzasadnij, dlaczego pasuje do działki i jej otoczenia. Dołącz dokumenty istotne w Twojej sprawie, np. decyzję o warunkach zabudowy, pozwolenie na budowę lub dokumentację istniejącej zabudowy. Dłuższe uzasadnienie możesz dołączyć jako załącznik do formularza.

Co to jest obszar uzupełnienia zabudowy (OUZ)?
To obszar, który gmina może wyznaczyć w planie ogóln

videos.title: „Jeśli ciągle mówisz, że nigdy nie zdradzisz, to zastanawiam się, czy właśnie o tym nie myślisz?“
videos.description:
Część osób, które zdradziły, nie szukała kogoś innego. Szukała innej wersji siebie.

Zaprosiłam Ameerę Ibrahim po raz kolejny, tym razem żeby porozmawiać o zdradzie inaczej niż zwykle. Nie o tym, kto jest winny ani jak wybaczyć. O tym, co się dzieje ZANIM cokolwiek się wydarzy. Dlaczego zdrada bywa doświadczeniem przebudzenia. Czy można zdradzić w dobrym związku z dobrym seksem. I dlaczego osoba, która głośno mówi „ja nigdy nie zdradziłam“, wcale nie powinna być taka pewna siebie.

W tym odcinku rozmawiamy o:
- myśleniu o zdradzie (i dlaczego to jeszcze nie jest zdrada)
- zdradzie spontanicznej vs. zaplanowanej, która boli bardziej?
- zdradzie emocjonalnej, która często nie ma nazwy, a niszczy bardziej niż fizyczna
- tym, czy „raz zdradził, zawsze będzie zdradzał“ to prawda
- kobietach, które zdradzają i dlaczego statystyki tego nie widać
- tym, co zdrada mówi o osobie, która jej dokonuje, a nie tylko o relacji

What happens when AI threatens your job, success no longer feels fulfilling, and your identity is built around being productive?

Why do so many high achievers struggle with self-worth, burnout, loneliness, and the feeling that they don't matter?

In this solo episode of Passion Struck, John R. Miles explores the Marketplace of Mattering and the hidden pressure to prove your worth through productivity, achievement, status, and external validation.

Drawing on behavioral science, psychology, human performance, and the science of mattering, John examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping the future of work, challenging our identities, and changing how we define human value. He explores the performance trap, conditional self-worth, leadership, personal fulfillment, and the disconnect between professional success and a meaningful life.

Most importantly, John introduces The Three Footholds: practical ways to reclaim personal agency, build genuine human connection, and help others feel seen, valued, and important.

In this episode, you'll discover:
-Why being productive and useful has become tied to our sense of self-worth.
-How artificial intelligence is changing work, identity, and human value.
-Why high achievement can still lead to burnout, loneliness, and emotional disconnection.
-What behavioral science reveals about external validation and the need to matter.
-How leadership and meaningful relationships influence human flourishing.
-Three practical ways to reclaim your purpose, strengthen relationships, and create a greater sense of mattering.

If you've ever questioned your purpose, felt defined by your achievements, or wondered whether you matter beyond what you do, this conversation is for you.

Explore more about The Mattering Effect: https://matteringeffect.com/

videos.title: How A Psychologist Predicts Divorce In 15 Minutes
videos.description:
A scientist in Seattle claimed he could predict divorce in just 15 minutes—not by watching a loud fight, but by spotting one tiny micro-expression. This is the untold story of John Gottman’s Love Lab psychology experiment and the real science behind relationship psychology and why marriages fail.

Most people assume dramatic arguments or big betrayals are the main signs of a failing marriage. Starting in the 1980s, psychologists John Gottman and Robert Levenson wired hundreds of couples to heart rate monitors, sweat sensors, and cameras behind a one-way mirror. By tracking physiological flooding and four specific communication traps—known as the Four Horsemen—they built a famous divorce prediction formula that reportedly reached over 90% accuracy.

In this video, we break down the controversial Love Lab experiment and what the internet quietly left out:

Why the first three minutes of an argument often predict how the entire conflict ends

The "Four Horsemen" communication traps: criticism, defensiveness, contempt, and stonewalling

How physiological flooding and racing heart rates hijack your brain during conflict

Why researchers and critics challenged the famous 90% divorce prediction claim

What actually decides if a couple survives: repair attempts and bids for connection

📌 Chapters:

0:46 Inside John Gottman's 1980s Lab Setup
1:27 Why the First 3 Minutes Predict Conflict

7:08 What Really Decides If a Couple Survives

Sources:

videos.title: Psychology of People Who Think Everyone Is Judging Them
videos.description:
Stop worrying about the psychology of people who think everyone is judging them. Learn why your mind creates these social scenarios and how to reclaim your focus.
Most of us feel like we are under a constant spotlight, acting as if someone is always watching our every move. This video explains the psychological concept behind this feeling, illustrating how we behave differently when we perceive external observation. By understanding these mental patterns, you can stop letting the fear of judgment dictate your daily choices.
We cover the specific studies on social perception and how our brains simulate the presence of others even when we are alone. You will learn how to navigate these psychological influences to reduce self-consciousness and gain a clearer perspective on your own mind.

videos.title: Dlaczego ktoś zostaje w przemocy, skoro tak bardzo cierpi? I Dominika Rosa
videos.description:
Życie jest piękne. Ale kiedy jesteś uwikłany w przemoc, trudno to zobaczyć. Jeszcze trudniej uwierzyć, że można coś zmienić.

W tym odcinku Dominika Rosa – mediatorka rodzinna i opiekunka rozwodowa – mówi o tym, jak świadomość może stać się początkiem wyjścia z przemocy. O odzyskiwaniu sprawczości, szukaniu pomocy i o tym, dlaczego osoba doświadczająca przemocy nie zawsze jest gotowa lub może po prostu „spakować się i odejść”.

Rozmawiamy także o tym, co dzieje się wtedy, gdy przemoc i konflikt dorosłych zaczynają dotykać dzieci. Dziecko nie powinno być żywą tarczą, zakładnikiem ani narzędziem w wojnie rodziców. To, czego doświadcza w domu, może wpływać na jego poczucie bezpieczeństwa, relacje i sposób radzenia sobie z emocjami.

Czy można przerwać ten schemat? Gdzie zaczyna się wolność? I co możemy zrobić, zanim przemoc stanie się doświadczeniem kolejnego pokolenia?

videos.channel: Britt Anderson Coaching /Mom Sweat Sanity Podcast
videos.description:
What if you could stop people-pleasing, set boundaries, and reset your life without feeling guilty?

Have you ever felt like you've spent so much time meeting other people's expectations that you've lost sight of what YOU actually want?

In today's episode of The Permission Series on The Mom Sweat Sanity Podcast, Brittany Anderson sits down with Karina Stampfli, founder of Compass Lifestyle + Fitness in North Vancouver, British Columbia, for an honest conversation about people-pleasing, setting boundaries, overcoming guilt, self-trust, and personal growth.

When asked, "What are you finally giving yourself permission to want?" Karina shares that she's ready to hit the reset button without feeling guilty about it.

After years of trying to keep the peace, avoiding confrontation, and prioritizing obligations, Karina has recognized that parts of her life no longer feel aligned with who she's becoming.

She's ready to make changes.

But as she shares, personal growth isn't always comfortable.

Sometimes the people around us have become accustomed to a particular version of who we are.

When we begin setting boundaries or choosing a different direction, not everyone will understand.

And sometimes that fear of disappointing others is exactly what keeps us stuck.

Together, Brittany and Karina discuss why women struggle with people-pleasing, how to recognize misalignment in your life, and what it takes to start making decisions that reflect your own values.

Karina also shares how reflecting on the past decade has reminded her of how much she's already grown, and why looking back can help us find confidence in what's still ahead.

One question from this conversation stands out:

But what if it works?

What if the change you're afraid to make turns out to be exactly what you need?

IN THIS EPISODE:

How to stop people-pleasing without feeling guilty
Setting healthy boundaries in relationships
Recognizing when your life feels out of alignment
Giving yourself permission to change and grow
Why other people's expectations can keep you stuck
Overcoming the fear of disappointing others
Learning to trust yourself during life transitions
Letting go of relationships and obligations that no longer fit
Building confidence through reflection and personal growth

videos.title: Fear of Judgment for Introverts: Why Fitting In Makes You Invisible
videos.description:
Stop conforming to others and start embracing your individuality. Being an introverted leader means finding the strength to stop hiding your true self.

Many of us feel a deep human need to belong, but that desire often leads to masking our personality to avoid judgment or rejection. When you constantly adjust your behavior to fit in, you diminish the unique perspective that makes your leadership style effective. This discussion examines how the fear of not fitting in stifles your potential and why authenticity is the best tool for connection.

Learning to stand in your own truth helps you move past the anxiety of what others think. By prioritizing your own values over external validation, you build a more sustainable approach to your work and personal life. True influence comes from showing up as you are rather than performing a version of yourself you think others want to see.Authentic leadership isn't about copying the people above you. It's about getting promoted for who you already are. In this episode of The Introverted Leader, CEO and keynote speaker Nikki Barua explains why introvert leadership works best when you stop trying to fit in. She also covers how to stand out at work using your quiet strengths, and why the traits you've been trying to fix are often your biggest edge.

Nikki calls herself a "painfully shy introvert." Early in her corporate career she wore pantyhose and pearls and played golf she hated, all to look like a leader. The more she fit in, she says, "the less there was of me to see." In high school she froze in front of 1,000 students and the whole auditorium laughed her off the stage. That day she decided she'd one day be paid to speak on stages around the world, and she did it without turning into a Tony Robbins-style performer.

Host Greg Weinger and Nikki talk about being yourself at work, getting past public speaking anxiety with thousands of reps, and why staying calm in a crisis earned her the nickname "wartime CEO." They also discuss quiet power: in a world full of AI-generated sameness, your presence, your patience and your lived story are what stand out. If you're doing great work and still feel invisible, or you've been told you need to be louder to get ahead, this conversation shows how to get seen and promoted without performing extroversion.

• Why copying the leaders above you makes you blend in, and what authentic leadership looks like in practice
• How to name your "zone of genius" and use it t

videos.title: The Psychology of Self-Sabotage (Why You Ruin Things Right Before They Get Good)
videos.description:
Three weeks of doing everything right… and then, one ordinary night, you blow it all up. Why?

Psychologists call it self-sabotage, and the strangest part is not that it happens — it's WHEN it happens. It almost never shows up when you're failing. It shows up right before things get good. In this video we find the hidden part of your brain that reaches for the brakes, using real psychology research.

In this video:
✅ The 1978 experiment where people chose a pill they were told would make them WORSE (Berglas & Jones)
✅ Why your brain would rather be certain about something bad than uncertain about something good (UCL, 2016)
✅ The inner "thermostat" that decides how much happiness you're allowed to feel (self-verification + the upper limit problem)
✅ The 4 respectable disguises of self-sabotage: procrastination, perfectionism, picking fights and the shrug
✅ 5 ways to break the loop — including the one question that works better than willpower

⏱️ Chapters

1:50 The Pill That Made People Worse
4:20 Your Brain Would Rather Know
6:38 The Thermostat Inside You

videos.title: Posłuchaj przed snem: jak chronić swój spokój przed zawiścią? | Carl Jung
videos.description:
Posłuchaj przed snem: jak chronić swój spokój przed zawiścią? | Carl Jung

Wracasz wieczorem do domu po dobrym dniu, kładziesz się do łóżka i nagle czujesz dziwny spadek sił, ciężkość w ciele i niepokój po jednej krótkiej rozmowie? Dawne kultury nazywały to „złym okiem” — ale Carl Gustav Jung w swoich dziełach „Aion” i „Archaiczny człowiek” przełożył to zjawisko na ścisły język psychologii głębi: cudza zawiść to wroga projekcja cienia i podprogowa sugestia, która potrafi wejść do Twojego umysłu tylko przez jedną furtkę.

W tym nocnym nagraniu (Carl Jung po polsku — do słuchania przed snem) odkryjesz, dlaczego człowiek zawistny nigdy nie nienawidzi Twoich wad, lecz własnego, nieprzeżytego „złotego cienia”, jak wyjąć wewnętrzny „haczyk psychiczny” fałszywej winy oraz jak uszczelnić swoją nieświadomość i energię psychiczną zanim zamkniesz oczy.

Spis treści tego wieczornego nagrania:
00:00 — Dziwny spadek sił po spotkaniu z ludźmi: psychologia „złego oka”
01:33 — Carl Jung („Aion”): dlaczego cudza zawiść szuka furtki w Twoim umyśle
03:46 — „Złoty cień”: czego tak naprawdę nienawidzi w Tobie osoba zawistna
10:14 — Haczyk psychiczny i podprogowa sugestia: jak cudza projekcja działa na sen
16:36 — Trzy przebrania ukrytej zawiści: fałszywa troska, zatruty komplement i chłód
20:01 — Królewska dyskrecja: jak chronić swój blask i granice emocjonalne
22:35 — Wieczorna praktyka przed snem: trzy ruchy zamykania kopuły umysłu
27:25 — Głęboki spokój i regenerujący sen bez cudzych projekcji

To nagranie sprawdzi się idealnie przed snem — pomaga osobom wrażliwym i empatycznym odciąć cudze emocje, uwolnić poczucie winy za własny rozwój i odzyskać czysty spokój wewnętrzny.

Zanim zamkniesz oczy, napisz w komentarzu jedno słowo: TARCZA — jako znak dla swojej podświadomości, że tej nocy chronisz swój spokój.

videos.title: Why Perfectionism Freezes You (It’s Not High Standards)
videos.description:
A blank page. A blinking cursor. A sentence you write, delete, and write again.

From the outside, it can look like laziness. From the inside, it often feels like caring too much to begin.

In this video, we explore the psychology of perfectionism and the difference between healthy high standards and the fear-driven need to get everything right. We look at how fear of judgment, self-worth tied to achievement, and the pressure of comparison can turn ordinary tasks into tests of personal value.

We also examine why avoiding unfinished work can feel like protection, how modern comparison can intensify the pressure to appear perfect, and what Stoic philosophy offers when outcomes and other people's opinions are beyond our control.

Drawing on the ideas of Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius, along with Voltaire's familiar warning that the best can become the enemy of the good and Herbert Simon's concept of satisficing, we consider how to pursue meaningful work without demanding perfection before we begin.

This isn't an argument for lowering every standard or ignoring responsibility. Some tasks genuinely require careful checking, precision, and high levels of accuracy. The challenge is learning when excellence serves the work, and when the fear of imperfection prevents the work from happening at all.

It's also important to recognize that not every difficulty with starting is perfectionism. Exhaustion, anxiety, low mood, and attention or executive-function difficulties, including those associated with ADHD, can play a role as well. These experiences can overlap, and persistent difficulties may deserve support from a qualified health professional.

The goal isn't to care less. It's to let your care take a form that allows you to move forward.

Sometimes, the first step toward good work is simply allowing the first version to exist.

Sources & Inspirations
Psychological research on perfectionistic strivings and perfectionistic concerns, self-worth and achievement; Stoic philosophy from Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius; Voltaire's reference to the idea that the best can be the enemy of the good; and Herbert Simon's concept of satisficing.

Disclaimer
This video is for educational and reflective purposes only. It is not medical or psychological advice, diagnosis, or treatment. It does not suggest that every difficulty with starting or completing tasks is caused by perfectionism.

The Bitcoin halving cycle put this peak right on schedule, and the window for the bottom opened and closed this month. Last week, on day 410 after the peak, Bitcoin closed at its lowest since June. The clock showed up on time. The ruler didn't.

videos.title: Is Cannabis bad for your mental health? This psychiatrist explains
videos.description:
How can you tell when something you do to cope is making life harder? When I ask a psychiatry resident how they talk to patients about cannabis, they offer a question you can ask yourself about any habit: “Is this helping or hindering?”

In this episode of Are You a Doctor? with Dr. Jeff Yoo, I meet a third-year psychiatry resident who explains what drew them to the specialty and why they wish more of us would give ourselves a break. We talk about what psychiatrists do, why they prescribe SSRI antidepressants alongside psychotherapy, and how the resident weighs the hopes and uncertainties around ketamine and psychedelics. They also share how seeing patients in the ER changed their perspective on cannabis, particularly high-potency products and the risk of psychosis.

The patient they still think about is a man in recovery from years of stimulant use. His social anxiety made it hard to leave home, yet at every appointment he was proud to share what he’d practiced since their last visit. Working with him challenged the resident’s own assumptions and shaped how they think about giving advice: start by understanding what the person in front of you wants to change.

videos.title: Debt Fund Losses Explained | Investors' Hangout with Dhirendra Kumar
videos.description:
Your gilt fund invests in government bonds, so why does it show a loss? This episode explains how interest rates move bond prices, and how to choose a debt fund that fits when you need the money.

In this episode of Investors' Hangout, brought to you by Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and Value Research, host Ruchira Sharma and Dhirendra Kumar look at why gilt funds have lost money over the last three months while liquid funds stayed positive. Dhirendra Kumar explains that a bond can be safe from default and still change in price.

When the policy rate rises, older bonds with lower interest become less valuable, and the longer the bond, the sharper the fall.

The discussion then turns to what a loss means in practice. He explains when a paper loss can become a real one, how target maturity funds work differently, and why long-duration funds suit only tactical investors. He then maps debt fund types to time frames, from liquid and money market funds for short needs to short-term funds for a few years. The episode ends with a rough guide to how much of a fall is worth worrying about.

In this episode, you will find answers to questions like:
- How can a fund that holds government bonds lose money?
- Why have some debt funds fallen more than others?
- Is my debt fund loss permanent?
- How do I choose a debt fund that matches my time frame?
- What are target maturity funds?
- When should a fall in a debt fund make me worry?

⚠️ Educational content only. Not financial advice. Investments carry market risks. Consult a certified advisor before investing.

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction 
01:00 Why Gilt Funds Showed a Loss
03:28 Why Bond Prices Fall When Rates Rise
05:36 Can gilt fund losses recover?
06:56 How to choose the right debt fund?

10:21 Planning for expenses in one to four years
10:44 Deciding whether to stay invested in or exit a loss-making debt fund
12:11 Key Takeaways
- Gilt funds carry interest-rate risk. Government backing makes default very unlikely, but it does not protect investors from falling bond prices when interest rates rise.
- Longer maturities mean steeper falls. Gilt funds can hold 20- to 30-year bonds. The longer the maturity, the sharper the price fall when interest rates rise.
- A paper loss can turn real. Higher yields can help recover losses, but heavy redemptions may force the fund to sell bonds at a loss.
- Match the fund to your time horizon. Liquid funds suit weeks or months,

videos.title: What nobody expects from Bitcoin in 2027
videos.description:
On November 19, Anthropic went public and raised $81.3 billion. Its employees couldn't stop smiling. The rest of the market, not so much: the Nasdaq sank, gold and silver fell, and Bitcoin broke the last model it had left standing.

So how do we value Bitcoin now? Digging through a pile of papers from the IMF, the Chicago Fed, Eugene Fama and others, I found three observations that change how, and to what, Bitcoin responds:

• From the October 2025 peak to June 2026, Bitcoin fell 53% while the S&P 500 rose 11%. Macro explains about 1% of that fall. The rest was Bitcoin.
• The 2023 rally wasn't risk appetite. Bitcoin simply stopped being scary, and that only happens once.
• The "leveraged Nasdaq" may have been a spurious correlation: the same money owning both things, from the ETFs to Harvard.

If Bitcoin is back to doing its own thing, what moves it? Miners, leverage and a bunch of religious zealots who never sell. Stanley Druckenmiller paints a hellish 2027, and the only model left that points up is the strangest one of all.

videos.title: Why Investors Buy Stocks High and Panic When They Go on Sale
videos.channel: Wallstreet Looks Like US Now Network
videos.description:
Tech stocks and semiconductor stocks just got hit hard—but that doesn’t automatically mean the opportunity is gone. In this video, I break down buying the dip, long-term investing, semiconductor stocks, NVIDIA, Micron, TSMC, Seagate, SanDisk, market psychology, and why patience matters more than prediction when great companies finally get cheaper.

The biggest mistake I see investors make is simple:

They want the stock at $1,000—but they’re scared of it at $500.

That makes no sense.

I walk through real examples of stocks that people chased near the highs, then wanted nothing to do with once they dropped 30%, 40%, 50% or more. The fundamentals may not have changed nearly as much as the price—but investor psychology changed completely.

We talk about why red feels more painful than green feels rewarding, why market turbulence can distort your thinking, and why I keep a long-term mindset instead of trying to predict every top and bottom.

I also explain why I’m still focused on buy and hold, why patience has created more wealth than constantly trying to time every move, and why I refuse to trade myself back into poverty chasing every short-term fluctuation.

Then I break down examples using Micron, SanDisk, TSMC, and Seagate to show how investor behavior changes as prices rise and fall—and why people often get most excited when the risk is highest and most fearful when discounts finally appear.

The goal is not to blindly buy everything that drops.

The goal is to have a blueprint, a process, and a long-term thesis so when the market gets irrational, your decision-making doesn’t become irrational with it.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Why Do Investors Want It Higher?

In this episode, Tom sits down with Zach Verwey, a therapist specializing in religious trauma, spirituality, and LGBTQ+ mental health, to explore how growing up in religious environments can impact queer people's sense of self, relationships, and connection.

They discuss how religious shame can follow queer people long after they've left the church, affecting intimacy, vulnerability, and their ability to form meaningful connections. Zach also unpacks the grief of leaving religion, including the loss of community, identity, and a framework for understanding the world.

The conversation also explores how psychedelics may support healing from religious trauma, why substance use can become a way to cope with shame and disconnection, and the importance of finding new sources of meaning, spirituality, and community.

Finally, Zach shares practical starting points for religious trauma recovery, from finding a supportive therapist and building meaningful connections to reconnecting with the body through embodiment practices. He reminds listeners that if they've been hurt by religion, their experiences are valid, they're not alone, and healing is possible.

About Zach:

Zach Verwey, MA, LPC specializes in providing mental health therapy to the LGBTQ+ community, with a focus on religious trauma, grief and loss, existential distress, psychedelic integration, and body image pressures. He sees clients at his private practice in Denver's Capitol Hill neighborhood and uses a relational approach, emphasizing empathy, trust, curiosity, and collaboration to support meaningful change. COED Y BRENIN SHOWCASE! 
100% WORTH A VISIT 🚵‍♂️🌲

What a fantastic day exploring Coed y Brenin – one of the UK’s most iconic mountain bike trail centres!

From incredible forest trails and flowing singletrack to rocky technical sections, stunning scenery and spectacular views, Coed y Brenin really does have something special to offer mountain bikers of all abilities.

In this video, we’re taking you on a full showcase of the venue – looking at the trails, the facilities, the visitor centre, the bike shop and what you can expect when you visit. We’ll also take a look at how Coed y Brenin has changed over the years and what the future might hold.

It’s a brilliant location with a huge amount to offer, and it’s sad to see the visitor centre no longer operating as it once did. Hopefully, a new opportunity will come along and we’ll see it reopen its doors, bringing that extra life and atmosphere back to this fantastic destination.

Let’s get behind Coed y Brenin! If you’ve never visited, put it on your list. If you’ve been before, why not come back for another ride? Supporting places like this helps keep mountain biking alive and thriving.

For me, it’s 100% worth a visit. Crack on and get it on your riding list!

videos.title: Diagnostyka w III kw. 2026: przychody +11,0% r/r, zysk netto −30,5% r/r, marża EBIT 13,2%
videos.description:
W III kwartale 2026 przychody Grupy Diagnostyka wyniosły 679,6 mln PLN, o 0,5% mniej q/q i o 11,0% więcej r/r. Zysk netto kwartału to 56,1 mln PLN, o 7,2% mniej q/q i o 30,5% mniej r/r, a marża EBIT 13,2%, czyli o 0,8 p.p. mniej q/q i o 3,3 p.p. mniej r/r. Średnia cena badania wzrosła o 8,3% r/r, ale koszty operacyjne rosły o 15,4% r/r, szybciej niż przychody w bazie III kwartału 2025 korekta CIT obniżyła podatek o 13,3 mln PLN. Na 30.09.2026 kredyty krótkoterminowe wynosiły 693,4 mln PLN wobec 6,1 mln PLN na 31.12.2025 – kredyty spółki dominującej są wymagalne w ciągu roku, a spółka negocjuje warunki finansowania.

Why do some men over 60 choose to remain single rather than return to a relationship? As men grow older, their priorities, expectations, and understanding of happiness can change. For some senior men, single life offers something they deeply value: peace of mind, independence, freedom, and the opportunity to focus on themselves.

In this video, Pillow Talks Psychology explores the advantages of being a single senior man and why some men over 60 decide that they do not want to return to traditional relationships. From enjoying personal freedom to protecting emotional well-being, discover how life after 60 can become an opportunity for growth, self-discovery, and a new definition of happiness.

Being single in your 60s does not automatically mean being lonely. For some men, it means having more control over their daily routines, finances, personal space, friendships, and future plans. Others may still value companionship and meaningful relationships. The key is understanding what genuinely brings you peace and fulfillment.

WHY MEN OVER 60 MAY CHOOSE TO STAY SINGLE

After decades of responsibilities, work, family commitments, or past relationship experiences, some men begin to value simplicity and independence more than ever. They may prefer spending time with friends, pursuing personal goals, enjoying quiet mornings, or making decisions without having to negotiate every aspect of daily life.

For other men, a loving relationship remains an important source of companionship, support, and happiness. There is no single right way to live after 60. What matters most is choosing a lifestyle that supports your emotional well-being, health, personal values, and long-term happiness.

videos.title: The only kind of man women respect — Robert Greene
videos.description:
The only kind of man women respect is not the man who constantly seeks their approval, but the man who understands human nature, masters his emotions, and knows his own worth. But what truly makes a man earn a woman's respect? And why do some men command respect without chasing attention, validation, or approval?

We don’t live in a world of pure logic; we live in a world of unresolved emotional histories, quiet anxieties, and deep-seated psychological needs. Behind every defensive reaction, every awkward romantic conflict, and every workplace tension lies a hidden struggle for validation, connection, and self-understanding.

If you want to understand **what makes a man respected by women** and navigate human relationships without falling into bitterness or illusion, you have to stop seeing people as rational actors or villains—and start seeing them as wounded, anxious creatures trying to protect themselves.

Drawing from the psychological frameworks of **Robert Greene, Alain de Botton, and The School of Life**, this is an anatomical breakdown of emotional maturity, masculine self-respect, love, and the complex laws of human nature.

Stop expecting perfection from fragile human beings—including yourself. Learn to decode emotional signals, master your own vulnerabilities, and replace blind judgment with strategic empathy. True respect begins with self-knowledge, emotional intelligence, and the ability to understand human nature.

"The only realistic course is to learn to forgive ourselves and others for being, in diverse ways, deeply flawed." — Alain de Botton

Key Themes Explored:

The Anatomy of Defense: Why people push away the exact connection they crave most.

Mastering Human Nature: Recognizing the hidden drives behind manipulation, charm, insecurity, and human behavior.

Strategic Empathy: Using self-knowledge to disarm conflict and navigate difficult personalities.

Emotional Resilience: Letting go of romantic idealism to build grounded, mature relationships and develop genuine self-respect.

The Psychology of Respect: Understanding emotional maturity, masculine confidence, and the qualities that build respect in relationships.

If you want to understand women, human nature, emotional intelligence, and the psychology behind genuine respect, this exploration of Robert Greene's principles offers a deeper perspective on relationships, self-awareness, and personal growth.

Nowy odcinek podcastu „Słuchając drogi” tworzonego przez Centrum Myśli Jana Pawła II jest już dostępny. 


Razem z moim rozmówcą, panem Jackiem Masłowskim, szukamy odpowiedzi na pytania o kondycje współczesnego mężczyzny. W trakcie naszego spotkania, próbujemy odpowiedzieć sobie m.in. na pytania; Jakie towarzyszą mu emocje? Skąd bierze się jego gigantyczne osamotnienie? Dlaczego zapomina o wspólnotowości i potrzebie siebie nawzajem? I jak może pozbyć się sztywnego gorsetu ról, które stały się już nieadekwatne? A także jak w przeszłości szukano męskości, a jak to odbywa się teraz? I o co chodzi z męską wrażliwością?


Mój rozmówca  jest psychologiem, psychoterapeutą, coachem, absolwentem filozofii na Wydziale Nauk Społecznych Uniwersytetu Śląskiego oraz Laboratorium Psychoedukacji, studiował psychologię w Szkole Wyższej Psychologii Społecznej oraz na Uniwersytecie Jagiellońskim, ukończył szkołę trenerów i terapeutów w Instytucie Terapii Gestalt w Krakowie, współzałożyciel i prezes Fundacji Masculinum - https://masculinum.org/

videos.title: When the Market Forces You to Sell: Wall Street in 1929, Bitcoin in 2026
videos.description:
A market can fall. But leverage can force people to sell — making the fall even harder to stop.
In 1929, brokers demanded more cash against falling stock collateral. In November 2026, crypto exchanges automatically closed leveraged Bitcoin futures positions. The technology is different. The pressure mechanism has a familiar shape.

This documentary compares the mechanics of the 1929 stock-market crash with the November 2026 Bitcoin derivatives selloff: margin, collateral, maintenance requirements, forced selling, liquidation cascades, and the limits of comparing two very different financial systems.

04:55 Bitcoin's November decline
05:48 Voluntary exit versus forced liquidation
06:30 How forced selling becomes a feedback loop
08:09 The rebound does not remove the risk
09:01 Where the comparison ends
